acc2177a-34e4-4941-93a2-b80bc18b8c91.name: 🎲 Fate & Chekhov Ledger
acc2177a-34e4-4941-93a2-b80bc18b8c91.content:
{{// 🎲 Chibi Fate & Chekhov Ledger: ARIA's world engine in about 470 tokens where the full edition spends 853, plus about 90 for its dice, plan, ledger and gate lines (those stay as they were). Every turn three hidden dice decide whether the world does something on its own and how close it lands to you. A picks the tier against the quiet streak q (AMBIENT texture, a MINOR hiccup or a rare MAJOR event); B decides whether the world acts on its own (TRUE) or something you did comes back through the [hot] Bullets, the setups that should pay off later (WEIGHTED); C picks the form (news, defer, complicate or displace a THREAD) and guards your scene: only MAJOR+TRUE on a natural 20 may harm it or stop or remove anyone present. A named future time becomes a TIME-LOCKED Bullet that fires on time, so Fate's appointments need ⏰ Time & Place. Fate never decides your next move. Its memory is the small folded 🎲 ledger at the end of each reply, which the preset's regex scripts dress up as the orange Fate & Routine panel: its field names, symbols, separators and order are untouched, and it has to stay in the chat. Chibi kept every dice ladder and threshold, the ages that matter (THREAD 8, Deferred 6, ripe World entry 8, Bullet 6 to fire and 12 to prune) and every ledger field, plus the tester fixes it could fit: q defined as AMBIENT turns in a row, a THREAD opened only when none is open and owned by the card's characters or you, displace defined, a no-warning MAJOR landing whole this turn, a ripe World entry landing whatever you are busy with, the one-sentence AMBIENT folded into a paragraph about someone present, news reaching the page only through someone present, and the natural-20 limit. It cut the rest: the World rule (your far-reaching acts logged unrolled, the cap of 5), Ambitions (stated goals counted to 5), the Quiet paragraph and the aftermath at q 0-2, the carried-state rule and 'intentions may fail', a MINOR reviving a Deferred item and a twice-deferred item returning as MAJOR, the age-4 first effect and age-12 fallback of World entries, Residue from every ended THREAD, the limit's extras (anyone Fate brings keeps to the edge, which the gate's People line also says) and most of the cell descriptions. Ships OFF in Chibi; best with 64k context and a model above 12B; pair it with ⏰ Time & Place.}}{{trim}}
{{setvar::ariaDice::Fate dice: A {{roll::1d20}} | B {{roll::1d20}} | C {{roll::1d20}}}}{{setvar::ariaFateLine::- Fate: A tier on q's band; B source; C form vs THREAD; cell; C 20 limit; results only.}}{{setvar::ariaLedgerLine::- Ledger: last 🎲 block plus this turn's changes, ages +1; the closing 🎲 block copies it.}}{{setvar::ariaLedgerGate::- Ledger: one full 🎲 block ends the reply.}}{{trim}}
{{user}} is always answered in full; prose names no mechanic.
Tier: A (-3 if MAJOR in the last 2 turns, else +4 at 3+ or +2 at 1-2 Deferred); q counts AMBIENT turns in a row. q 0-2: MINOR 16+, MAJOR 20+; q 3-6: 12+, 19+; q 7+: 8+, 17+; below MINOR: AMBIENT, q+1; else q 0.
Source: hp = [hot] Bullets; WEIGHTED at B 14+ (hp 1-2), 9+ (3-4), 5+ (5+), else TRUE.
Form, C once at the tier's line: AMBIENT 1-6 World news, shown only once it reaches someone present, instead of its cell. No THREAD: MINOR/MAJOR opens one, a pursuit of the card's characters or {{user}}. THREAD open: MINOR 1-12 defers, else complicates; MAJOR 1-10 complicates, else displaces (parks it, opens one on the happening). THREAD closes or parks by age 8 and Deferred expires at 6.
TRUE | WEIGHTED:
AMBIENT: one sentence of texture, folded into a paragraph about someone present | a [hot] Bullet warms, +1 extra age.
MINOR: small cost/pleasure, or news moves a World entry a band toward LOCAL | a consequence brushes {{user}}.
MAJOR, rare, whole this turn: a REGIONAL/LOCAL World entry aged 8+ lands as Residue however busy {{user}} is; none: someone else's large, arbitrary happening, unwarned | the heaviest, then oldest [hot] Bullet aged 6+ fires (none: TRUE).
Only MAJOR+TRUE on C 20 may harm {{user}}'s scene or close circle, or stop/remove anyone present; else all stay and carry on, harm and LOCAL events arrive from outside.
Bullets (max 8): load ≤1 a turn, [hot] if {{user}} caused it; prune at 12. A named future time loads an ageless TIME-LOCKED one at Day # HH:MM, firing on time at any tier.
Ledger (none if empty): <details><summary>🎲</summary>q: n | hp: n | thread: pursuit, age n | deferred: item xN, age n | world: event, ELSEWHERE/REGIONAL/LOCAL, age n | bullets: setup [hot], weight 1-3, age n | ambitions: goal n/5 | residue: lasting change | last: AMBIENT/MINOR/MAJOR TRUE/WEIGHTED, fate's 5-word happening</details>

G5 world engine: ⏰ Time & Place (5dcccd11), 🎲 Fate & Chekhov Ledger (acc2177a), 🥰 Bonds Lite (5506d699). This file is the primary. Two alternatives sit beside it in the drafts folder: G5.floor.json (the least the numbers and the biggest tester fixes allow) and G5.full.json (every mechanic of the snapshot in Chibi wording).

RESULT. skeleton.py is OK for all three prompts; no JB addition touches this group, so no skeleton difference is intended. The three TC blocks (tc.time_place_block, tc.fate_block, tc.bonds_block: the text between each module's {{#if}} and {{/if}} in the snapshot TC) are OK under skeleton.py --text. The frozen checker (analyse_cc and analyse_tc on in-memory copies of the snapshot with these texts swapped in, alone and together with the G1 to G4 drafts) finds no wiring, order or cache error; its only two reports are the JB-order ones the pre-JB snapshot has. The regex-facing text is byte-for-byte the snapshot's, compared by script: the 🎲 template (308 characters), Fate's setvar run (dice with {{roll::1d20}}, plan, ledger and gate lines), Bonds' setvar run with both #if branches, the Name↔Name +6/3/0 (BOND/Sparks/Grudge) pair legend and "Touch gates:"; the header shape [🕰️ … ] still matches the Impersonate strip scripts.
tok.py, plain and with {"ariaLedgerLine":"x"} (same own-text figures): Time & Place 50 (ceiling 45); Fate & Chekhov Ledger 470 (300); Bonds Lite 210 (120). Lines, verbatim from the snapshot and already under their ceilings: dice 7 + plan 22 + ledger 26 + gate 33 = 88 (ceiling 110; 61 with Fate alone), Bonds plan line 24 (30). Group: 50 + 470 + 210 + 88 + 24 = 842 against the ceilings' sum of 605, so +237. Every own-text row is over; please read the next paragraph before cutting.

WHY THE CEILINGS CANNOT HOLD. (1) The snapshot's modules are already dense. Every mechanic of the three in Chibi wording (G5.full.json: the primary plus every restore item) measures 81 + 738 + 253 own and the same 112 for the lines, 1,184 in all, against the snapshot's 82 + 853 + 297 + 112 = 1,344: Douyin wording saves 12% when nothing is dropped. Time & Place has no fat at all (81 against 82). The ceilings' sum is 45% of the snapshot, so meeting it means dropping more than half of the mechanics. (2) Even the floor (G5.floor.json) misses every row: 48 + 381 + 192 + 112 = 733 against 605. It has no World, Ambitions, Quiet, aftermath, carried-state, revive, age-4, age-12 or Residue text, one-line cells, the limit cut to its core, Bonds' scale cut to its extremes and only the biggest tester fixes. Fate there still holds principle 14, Tier 53, Source 21, Form 69, cells 78, limit 23, Bullets and TIME-LOCKED 38 and the ledger 83. The 🎲 template with its prefix is 83 alone, 28% of the 300, and stays byte-for-byte because the Fate panel regexes read it. Getting under 300 would also cost the Bullets (the Chekhov half of the module and the only source of hp) or the natural-20 limit; Bonds' pair legend 34 + Touch gates 28 + Sparks, Grudge and conversions 95 already make 157 against 120. Those are the items the spec lists as must-keep (Fate's dice tiers, ladders and ledger fields; Bonds' gates, Sparks, Grudge and conversions). (3) The cap. With the G1 to G4 drafts swapped into the snapshot (everything ON, Tags on), G6 at its ceilings (407) and the JB at 55, the estimate for the whole Chibi is 3,039 with this primary, 2,930 with the floor and 3,381 with the full set, against the 3,000 cap and the 2,850 aim; the aim would need G5 at about 650, under the floor (733). So this primary keeps the mechanics and tester fixes the spec names and goes over by as little as that allows, and its cut menu is how to take the cap from G5 if G6 and the JB hold their ceilings (K1 to K9, -44, estimate about 2,995). The restore menu is the other direction; restoring all of it is the full set.
